surface: Links autoLink draws in cells: a URL beside an opted-out one, a link inside a sentence, an email link, a HYPERLINK formula's label, and opening a link with Alt+Enter.

steps.note: B1 holds a URL in a column that opts out of autoLink (`autoLink: false`): plain text, no link. A group cannot require an absence, so the goldens show whether a reader says `link` here. The groups ask for one word of each URL (`optout`, `one`, `someone`), because a reader spells the punctuation of a URL its own way (`example dot com slash one`).

A1 holds `https://example.com/one`, which autoLink wraps in a link: the cell's text and the link role. Column D's user link is left out of the scenario, because its text, `user link`, would satisfy the link group on its own.
A2 holds a sentence with a URL in the middle, `Visit https://example.com/two for details.`: the text around the link and the link role.
A3 holds `mailto:someone@example.com`. The grid hides the `mailto:` prefix from view, so the link reads as the address.
F1 holds `=HYPERLINK("https://example.com/hf", "HF label")`: a link whose name is its label, not its URL.
A7 holds a link to a page of the same server (`/tests/fixtures/demo/grid.html`), which the next step opens, so the run stays offline.

Alt+Enter opens the selected cell's first link in a new tab (autoLink's default target, `_blank`). The reader follows the new tab and reads its title. The last step, because the focus stays on the new tab; the test's browser context closes it.
